messages.subject: Multivariate GPs
parts:
I'm about to push a bunch of changes which I will describe in a series
of emails. The work, done over the past week or so, come together to
make Stan much faster in a number of ways (any models using multI_* or
*wishart distributions should be much faster), and in particular,
greatly improves the ability to work with Gaussian Process models.

Next up we have...

2) Multivariate Gaussian Processes

I've added (actually completed to be precise) the multi_gp_log
function. It is best explained with an example:

matrix[yDim,N] y; // matrix of outputs
matrix[N,N] K; // kernel matrix
vector[yDim] w; // individual scales for each output dimension

for (i in 1:yDim)
row(y,i) ~ multi_normal(zeros,(1/w[i])*K));

With multi_gp_log, the above can be done much more efficiently and
compactly with:

y ~ multi_gp(K,w);

I've added some rudimentary tests, although they're probably not as
comprehensive they should be. Currently there is no documentation.
If someone wants to expand the GP section of the manual to describe
this, that would be awesome. Otherwise, it may take me a while to do
it.


2.5) GP Kernel computation

I've implemented a squared_dist function and vari, which makes
computing a squared exponential kernel more efficient. Instead of:

K[i,j] <- exp(-alpha*dot_self(col(x,i) - col(x,j)));

you can write

K[i,j] <- exp(-alpha*squared_dist(col(x,i),col(x,j)));

which saves a fair amount of varis since this line would be executed
O(N^2) times. I've implemented unit tests for the squared_dist
function, but no documentation yet.

Cheers,
Marcus
